successors.name: Portuguese Empire
successors.text: Kilwa Kisiwani, where the Portuguese built Fort Santiago in 1505, and the dependencies they claimed

ledger.x: 957: Ali ibn al-Hassan Shirazi founds the sultanate of Kilwa.
c. 1277: the Mahdali dynasty of Yemeni Arabs replaces the Shirazi. 'End of Persian Shirazi dynasty c. 1277, beginning of Mahdali dynasty of Yemeni Arab'; same state, same colour.
Early 14th century: Mombasa becomes a dependency of Kilwa.
c. 1495: the Mahdali line ends. 'End of Mahdali dynasty c. 1495, beginning of a series of usurpers and Portuguese puppets.'
1505: Almeida's fleet takes Kilwa and builds Fort Santiago.
1505: the island dependencies slip away with the Portuguese conquest.
1513: the sultanate is disestablished (infobox 'Disestablished: 1513') and the land passes to the Portuguese Empire.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Kilwa
wars.outcome: Portuguese victory: Almeida's fleet entered the harbour in 1505, Fort Santiago was built and a garrison left; by late 1506 the Portuguese were convening 'competing sultans Micante and Hussein'.

certainty.note: An island city-state with claimed dependencies: no boundary or survey on the page.
